_README: Preset for the onset-asynchrony task run as RISING FIGURE vs PLAIN CLOUD.
orders        ['rising']    one present condition: the element ascends in frequency.
absent_class  'plain'       a 'no' trial has NO element structure at all. Same 30 channels,
same per-channel budget, same total tone count -- every tone
placed at a free time at random. Nothing starts together
anywhere. This is the classic figure-vs-cloud contrast, and it
is the only absent class where the question 'was a figure
there?' means what it says.
WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHAT THE DENSITY IS FOR. Synchrony is an envelope event: seven tones
starting together are a level event a flat cloud does not have, and no arrangement of the
same tones avoids it. At the pilot's density (28 tones per channel) a learnt observer reads
this contrast at d' = +2.60, 90% correct, WITHOUT hearing anything group -- it leaks at every
rung. The one lever that works is burying the event in a denser cloud, and it works well:
tones/channel   occupancy   mean tones sounding   learnt d'   % correct
So from 8 ms up this is clean, 4 ms is marginal, and 0 ms cannot be cleaned at any density --
a simultaneous group IS a level event, and 0 ms is the rung that means 'simultaneous'. Treat
0 ms as a manipulation check, not a data point, and report the table beside the ladder.
The density is a trade, not a free win: it also masks the figure. 52 leaves the figure among
~14 simultaneous tones instead of ~8. Listen at several before committing --
python -m seqsfg asynchrony-demo --preset asynchrony_plain_config.json --set tones_per_channel=28
... and 40, 52, 64 -- and pick by ear. tone_amplitude is lowered with it to stay clear of
clipping; recalibrate when you change either.
asynchrony_config.json (roving, two orders) and asynchrony_rising_config.json (roving, rising)
are untouched, and so is pilot_config.json.
